To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a system that combines existing astronomical source detection software with machine learning algorithms to automatically detect humans and animals from thermal infrared aerial footage.

we have developed a novel, automated, end-to-end software pipeline that combines astronomical source detection software with machine learning algorithms to efficiently and reliably identify animals in thermal infrared video footage taken by unmanned aerial vehicles.

we have developed an unmanned aerial system and associated software pipeline that can reliably and efficiently detect humans and animals, including endangered species, in thermal infrared footage and we have demonstrated how the software can be used to assess the completeness of different datasets to different types of objects as a function of observing conditions, etc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, multi disciplinary, automated system for the monitoring of endangered animal populations using unmanned aerial systems.
the use of unmanned aerial systems to monitor animal populations.
developing an automated pipeline to detect animals in thermal infrared aerial footage, and using this pipeline to estimate the completeness and efficiency of different observational datasets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pipeline we have developed is capable of automatically detecting humans and animals in video footage taken with an unmanned aerial system.

we have developed a system that uses freely available astronomical source finding software to detect animals in aerial thermal video footage and that this system has been successfully tested on aerial video footage taken at a controlled, field site.
we have successfully adapted astronomical source detection software for use in the detection and analysis of aerial thermal infrared footage of animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the astronomical source detection software is very useful to detect animals from aerial thermal infrared video footage.

the software pipeline we have developed is able to detect animals in aerial thermal images with a precision and accuracy comparable to that of humans and that it can be used as a tool to estimate completeness of aerial surveys as a function of a number of different parameters.
this project was an interdisciplinary effort that used the skills and expertise of astronomers to solve an important problem in wildlife conservation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the astronomical source detection software is well suited to the task of detecting animals in aerial footage and can be used to efficiently and reliably extract useful information from large amounts of aerial video footage.

the expertise and software developed for astronomical applications can be adapted and applied to other problems, and in particular to the monitoring of animals in the wild, where the ability to detect and track individual animals from a distance is a key requirement.

the astronomical community has a wealth of experience and software tools that can be used to tackle problems outside of astronomy, in particular in conservation science, where the need for automated analysis of large amounts of data is increasing rapidly.
